title: OOMKilled — payments-api keeps dying
intro: Alerts fired for payments-api. Pods keep restarting but there's nothing obvious in the app logs.

steps.fake_output:
NAME                          READY   STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE
payments-api-6b7f8d9c-lm2np   0/1     OOMKilled   7          20m

steps.prompt: Get the full details to confirm the reason.
steps.fake_output:
Last State: Terminated
  Reason: OOMKilled
  Exit Code: 137
Limits:
  memory: 128Mi
Requests:
  memory: 64Mi
steps.hint: describe will show the termination reason and the configured memory limit.

steps.prompt: Check actual memory usage against that limit.
steps.hint: kubectl top shows live resource usage.

steps.prompt: The app is using ~310Mi but the limit is only 128Mi. Patch the deployment to raise the memory limit to 512Mi.
steps.hint: You can patch it directly, or use kubectl edit to open it in your editor and change the memory limit under resources.limits.

steps.prompt: Watch the rollout to confirm the fix is deploying.
steps.fake_output:
Waiting for deployment "payments-api" rollout to finish...
deployment "payments-api" successfully rolled out
steps.hint: rollout status blocks until the update finishes.

resolution: The container's actual memory usage (310Mi) exceeded its configured limit (128Mi), so the kernel OOM-killed it every time it hit that ceiling — this is exit code 137, always worth recognizing immediately. Setting limits too low based on old traffic assumptions is one of the most common real-world causes of mystery restarts. Also worth noting: this only fixes the symptom — if 310Mi usage itself was a memory leak, that still needs investigating separately.
